ukmt-stmc-2018-19-final-group-01.prompt: Find the value of $$\frac{2020!+2019!}{2019!}+\frac{2019!+2018!}{2018!}+\frac{2018!+2017!}{2017!}.$$ (The notation $n!$ means the product of all the positive integers from $1$ to $n$.)

ukmt-stmc-2018-19-final-group-02a.prompt: A square measuring $11$ cm by $11$ cm has been divided into five rectangles, one of which is shaded, as shown in the diagram. Four of the rectangles, including the shaded rectangle, have perimeter $20$ cm. What, in cm, is the perimeter of the rectangle that does not have perimeter $20$ cm?

ukmt-stmc-2018-19-final-group-02b.prompt: A square measuring $11$ cm by $11$ cm has been divided into five rectangles, one of which is shaded, as shown in the diagram. Four of the rectangles, including the shaded rectangle, have perimeter $20$ cm. What, in $\text{cm}^2$, is the area of the shaded rectangle?

ukmt-stmc-2018-19-final-group-03.prompt: The expression $$(3^{20}-3^{19})(3^{20}-3^{18})(3^{20}-3^{17})(3^{20}-3^{16})(3^{20}-3^{15})(3^{20}-3^{14})$$ can be written in index form as $2^a\times3^b\times5^c\times7^d\times11^e\times13^f$. What is the value of $a+b+c+d+e+f$?

ukmt-stmc-2018-19-final-group-04.prompt:
The $n$th term of a sequence is $u_n$. The sequence is defined for each positive integer $n$ as follows: $u_1=a$ and, for $n\ge1$,
$$u_{n+1}=\begin{cases}\text{the sum of the previous } n \text{ terms} & \text{if } n \text{ is even},\\ \text{the sum of the previous } \tfrac12(n+1)\text{ terms} & \text{if } n \text{ is odd}.\end{cases}$$
You are given that $u_9=800$. What is the value of $a$?

ukmt-stmc-2018-19-final-group-05.prompt: An office supplier sells files for one price, staplers for a different price, and boxes of paper clips for a third price. One small business buys $20$ files, $19$ staplers and $18$ boxes of paper clips. The total cost of these items is £52. A second small business buys $5$ files, $2$ staplers and $19$ boxes of paper clips. The total cost of these items is £21. A third small business buys $50$ files, $53$ staplers and $16$ boxes of paper clips. What is the total cost of the items that the third business buys?

ukmt-stmc-2018-19-final-group-06a.prompt: Consider the sequence of shapes shown. There are two squares of any size in the first shape of the sequence. There are seven squares of any size in the second shape of the sequence: six $1\times1$ squares and one $2\times2$ square. There are sixteen squares of any size in the third shape in the sequence: twelve $1\times1$ squares and four $2\times2$ squares. How many squares of any size are there in the fourth shape of the sequence?

ukmt-stmc-2018-19-final-group-06b.prompt: Consider the sequence of shapes shown. There are two squares of any size in the first shape of the sequence. There are seven squares of any size in the second shape of the sequence: six $1\times1$ squares and one $2\times2$ square. There are sixteen squares of any size in the third shape in the sequence: twelve $1\times1$ squares and four $2\times2$ squares. How many squares of any size are there in the ninth shape of the sequence?

ukmt-stmc-2018-19-final-group-07.prompt: A five-digit integer '$abcde$' has five different non-zero digits. It has the property that it is divisible by the product of its digits. $13248$ is an example of such a number since $1\times3\times2\times4\times8=192$ and $13248=192\times69$. What is the greatest five-digit integer with this property?

ukmt-stmc-2018-19-final-group-08.prompt: $ABCD$ is a square. Points $Q,R,S$ and $T$ are the midpoints of sides $AB,BC,CD$ and $DA$, respectively. A point $X$ is chosen in the interior of the square such that the areas of the quadrilaterals $BRXQ$, $CSXR$ and $DTXS$ are $42$, $35$ and $30$, respectively. What is the area of the triangle $QXT$?

ukmt-stmc-2018-19-final-group-09.prompt:
Alex, Beatrice, Charmian and Denzil are four children. Each of them either always tells the truth or always tells lies. One day they make the following statements:
- Alex: 'Beatrice always tells lies.'
- Beatrice: 'Alex and Denzil are either both truth tellers or both liars.'
- Charmian: 'Beatrice and Denzil are either both liars or both truth tellers.'
- Denzil: 'I always tell the truth.'
Who is definitely lying?

ukmt-stmc-2018-19-final-group-10.prompt: There are two pairs of positive integers $(x,y)$ that satisfy the equation $x^2y-xy^2=286$. Find both pairs. (Give each pair in the form $(x,y)$; the order of the two pairs does not matter.)
